## Astronomical 0.2.85
### Expert warmth that survives restarts
For sparse-MoE models served from storage, the per-model expert usage history now keeps phase-separated prefill and decode evidence, ages old evidence with a one-generation half-life, and uses decode evidence alone to pre-warm tables. A model you use regularly starts measurably warmer with every launch instead of remembering only the last request. The history file beside streamed MoE artifacts upgrades to format 2; the first launch after upgrading starts that model cold once, and warmth accumulates from then on.
### Lighter, faster builds; ring crypto for downloads
The Amazon `aws-lc` crypto dependency is gone: model downloads run over rustls with the ring provider installed at the transport layer, and builds no longer compile AWS libcrypto — removing the single largest build unit. Third-party notices no longer carry aws-lc entries.
### Serving measurements you can trust
Durable throughput records now carry the completion's ordinal within its worker, so first-touch rates and warmed rates can never be silently compared as one series, and the streaming prefill floor reflects the current fresh-session calibration.
### Under the hood
Code-shape enforcement (complexity ratchet, function-length budget) moved entirely to pre-commit; SwiftPM cache self-eviction fixed and the sccache budget raised; a workspace-wide function-length and readability paydown; acceptance-battery defect fixes; and a nightly notices freshness lane.
Compatibility: configuration format unchanged; existing model directories, catalogs, and instance state are preserved. No REST/IPC surface changes.
